Market sentiment faced additional headwinds after U.S. President Donald Trump threatened sweeping tariffs or a partial trade halt against the European Union over its proposal to grant Canada "associate member" status.
Despite these headwinds, U.S. equity index futures pointed toward a morning rebound, with Nasdaq futures up 0.67%, S&P 500 futures gaining 0.59%, and Dow futures rising 0.61%.

Geopolitical focus temporarily shifted to energy supply security as crude oil prices moderated around $102 per barrel on expectations that Saudi Arabia would restore flows through its East-West pipeline, while spot gold advanced toward $4,300 per ounce.
South Korea’s KOSPI rose 0.66% to around 6,755, extending gains from the previous session. The South Korean won weakened to around 1,380 per dollar.

On the corporate front, BYD fell 0.6% after reports that Chinese officials may include the automaker in Xi Jinping’s business delegation for his summit with Trump.
